questions.question: Explain why women's work changed during the First World War.
questions.expected_answer: Before 1914 many working-class women worked in domestic service, textiles and shops, and middle-class women as teachers, nurses and clerks, usually leaving work on marriage, with lower pay and the ideal of separate spheres. Total war took millions of men into the forces and created huge demand for weapons, food and transport; the shell crisis of 1915 led to the Ministry of Munitions under Lloyd George. Trade unions accepted dilution for the duration of the war, and the 1915 women's right to serve march, led by the Pankhursts, pressed for women to be employed.

questions.question: Describe the different kinds of work women did during the war.
questions.expected_answer: About nine hundred thousand munitionettes by 1918 produced most of the army's shells, working long shifts with TNT that turned skin yellow, the canaries, and facing explosions such as Barnbow in 1916 and Silvertown in 1917, but earning more than in domestic service. Women worked in engineering, shipbuilding, transport, offices and police patrols; the Women's Land Army of 1917 worked farms; the WAAC, WRNS and WRAF did non-combat jobs; nurses and VADs, the FANY and the Scottish Women's Hospitals of Dr Elsie Inglis cared for the wounded, and Edith Cavell was executed in 1915.

questions.question: How far did the war change women's position in the workplace?
questions.expected_answer: Women in paid work rose from about 5.9 to about 7.3 million, roughly 24 percent, and women proved they could do skilled and heavy work. But women were usually paid less than men, most munitions and many industrial workers lost their jobs after 1918, the 1919 Restoration of Pre-War Practices Act restored men's jobs and the marriage bar continued. Lasting changes included fewer women in domestic service, more in offices and light industry, the 1919 Sex Disqualification (Removal) Act and votes for some women in 1918. Historians debate the extent of change; a balanced view sees both progress and limits.
